title: WCAG 2.2 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
description: W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level A and AA success criteria. WCAG 2.2 extends WCAG 2.1 with additional success criteria to improve accessibility, particularly for users with cognitive disabilities and mobile device users.

A.description: Level A (Minimum) - The most basic web accessibility features. If this level is not satisfied, some groups will find it impossible to access information on the website.

AA.description: Level AA (Mid-Range) - Deals with the biggest and most common barriers for disabled users. This is the level most organizations should strive for and is legally required in many jurisdictions.

AAA.description: Level AAA (Highest) - The highest level of accessibility. Not required for entire sites but may be applied to specific pages or sections.

principles.name: Perceivable
principles.description: Information and user interface components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive.

guidelines.name: Text Alternatives
guidelines.description: Provide text alternatives for any non-text content so that it can be changed into other forms people need, such as large print, braille, speech, symbols or simpler language.

success_criteria.name: Non-text Content
success_criteria.description: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.
success_criteria.intent: To make information conveyed by non-text content accessible through the use of text alternatives. Text alternatives can be presented in a variety of ways (visually, audibly, or tactilely) to match the needs of the user.
exceptions: Controls and Input: If non-text content is a control or accepts user input, it has a name that describes its purpose
Time-Based Media: If non-text content is time-based media, text alternatives provide descriptive identification
Test: If non-text content is a test that would be invalid if presented in text, text alternatives provide descriptive identification
Sensory: If non-text content is primarily intended to create a specific sensory experience, text alternatives provide descriptive identification
CAPTCHA: Text alternative identifies purpose, and alternative forms for different disabilities are provided

Decoration, Formatting, Invisible: If non-text content is pure decoration, used only for visual formatting, or not presented to users, it is implemented in a way that can be ignored by assistive technology

sufficient: Using alt attribute on img elements (H37)
Using null alt text and no title attribute on img elements for decorative images (H67)
Providing a text alternative for non-text content using aria-label (ARIA6)
Providing a text alternative using aria-labelledby (ARIA10)
Using longdesc attribute for complex images (H45)
Providing a long description in text near the image (G73, G74)
Using figure and figcaption elements (H88)
advisory: Providing text alternatives for emojis and emoticons
Using SVG with title and desc elements
failures: Using alt attribute text that is not equivalent (F30)
Using generic or placeholder alt text (F39)
Omitting alt attribute on img elements (F65)

test_procedures: Identify all non-text content (images, icons, charts, graphics)
Verify that each has a text alternative that serves equivalent purpose
Check that decorative images have empty alt attributes
Verify CAPTCHA has text alternative and accessible alternatives provided
Confirm complex images have detailed descriptions via longdesc, aria-describedby, or adjacent text
Test with screen reader to ensure alternatives are read correctly

common_failures.example: with no alt attribute
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users cannot access content

common_failures.example: alt='image' or alt='photo'

common_failures.issue: Alt text contains 'image of' or 'picture of'
common_failures.example: alt='image of a cat'
common_failures.impact: Redundant information as screen reader already announces it as image

common_failures.example: Background pattern has detailed alt text
common_failures.impact: Creates noise for screen reader users

guidelines.name: Time-based Media
guidelines.description: Provide alternatives for time-based media (audio and video).

success_criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
success_criteria.description: For prerecorded audio-only and prerecorded video-only media, alternatives are provided that present equivalent information.
success_criteria.intent: To make information conveyed by prerecorded audio-only and video-only media available to all users, including those who are deaf, hard of hearing, blind, or have low vision.

sufficient: Providing a transcript for audio-only content (G158)
Providing an audio track for video-only content (G159)
Providing a text document including descriptions of major visual elements and transcript of dialogue (G166)
advisory: Linking to text transcripts from audio/video
failures: No alternative provided for prerecorded audio-only (F30)
No alternative provided for prerecorded video-only (F67)

test_procedures: Identify all prerecorded audio-only content
Verify transcript is provided that includes all audio information
Identify all prerecorded video-only content
Verify audio track or text description is provided
Check that alternatives convey equivalent information

common_failures.example: Audio podcast with no text alternative
Transcript missing sound effects or non-speech audio

success_criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
success_criteria.description: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
success_criteria.intent: To enable people who are deaf or hard of hearing to watch synchronized media presentations. Captions provide the part of the content available via the audio track.

sufficient: Providing closed captions using video player caption features (G87)
Providing open captions embedded in the video (G93)
Using WebVTT for captions (H95)
Using SMIL to add captions (SM11, SM12)
advisory: Using captions that are synchronized within 150ms
failures: No captions provided for video with audio (F8)
Captions not synchronized with audio (F74)
Captions missing important audio information (F75)

test_procedures: Identify all prerecorded synchronized media (video with audio)
Verify captions are provided
Check that captions include all dialogue
Verify captions include relevant sound effects
Check synchronization of captions with audio
Confirm caption controls are accessible

common_failures.example: YouTube auto-captions with errors
Dialogue captioned but not [door slams] or [phone ringing]

success_criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
success_criteria.description: An alternative for time-based media or audio description of the prerecorded video content is provided for synchronized media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
success_criteria.intent: To provide people who are blind or visually impaired access to the visual information in a synchronized media presentation.

sufficient: Providing audio description (G78)
Providing a full text alternative including descriptions of visual information (G173)
Using extended audio description (G8)
advisory: Providing audio description for live video
failures: No audio description or alternative provided (F81)

test_procedures: Identify prerecorded video with synchronized audio
Check if visual information is described in audio
If not, verify a full text transcript with visual descriptions exists
Confirm important visual details are included

common_failures.example: Video shows process but audio doesn't describe steps
common_failures.impact: Blind users miss critical visual information

success_criteria.name: Captions (Live)
success_criteria.description: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.
success_criteria.intent: To enable people who are deaf or hard of hearing to watch real-time presentations by providing captions of the audio content.

sufficient: Using real-time text captioning service (G9, G87)
Providing captions using video player that supports captions (SM11, SM12)
failures: No captions for live video content (F8)

test_procedures: Identify all live audio/video content
Verify real-time captions are provided
Check caption accuracy (allowing for real-time limitations)
Verify captions keep pace with audio

common_failures.example: Live streaming event with no captioning service
common_failures.impact: Deaf users excluded from live events

success_criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
success_criteria.description: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content in synchronized media.
success_criteria.intent: To provide people who are blind or visually impaired access to the visual information in a synchronized media presentation (stronger requirement than 1.2.3).

sufficient: Providing audio description for video (G78)
Providing extended audio description (G173)
Using SMIL to add audio description (SM6, SM7)
advisory: Providing audio description in multiple languages
failures: Important visual information not described in audio (F81)

test_procedures: Identify all prerecorded video with audio
Verify audio description track is available
Check that all important visual information is described
Test with screen off to ensure understanding is possible from audio alone

common_failures.example: Only some visual elements described, not all
common_failures.impact: Blind users miss important visual context

guidelines.name: Adaptable
guidelines.description: Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure.

success_criteria.name: Info and Relationships
success_criteria.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that information and relationships that are implied by visual or auditory formatting are preserved when the presentation format changes (e.g., when read by a screen reader, or when CSS is not loaded).

sufficient: Using semantic HTML elements (H49, H51, H71, H85)
Using ARIA roles, states, and properties (ARIA11, ARIA12, ARIA13)
Using table headers for data tables (H43, H63)
Using fieldset and legend for form groups (H71)
Using label elements for form controls (H44)
Using heading elements (H42)
Using list elements for lists (H48)
advisory: Using CSS for visual presentation rather than HTML tables
Providing semantic markup for emphasized text
failures: Using presentation markup instead of structural markup (F43, F46)
Not using header elements for headings (F2)
Using white space characters to format tables (F49)
Using tables for layout (F48, F92)

test_procedures: View page with CSS disabled and verify structure is clear
Check that headings use h1-h6 elements
Verify lists use ul, ol, or dl elements
Check data tables use th elements and scope or headers attributes
Verify form controls have associated labels
Test with screen reader to confirm relationships are announced
Check that visual formatting conveys structure programmatically

common_failures.example:
Heading
instead of

Heading
common_failures.impact: Screen readers cannot navigate by headings

common_failures.example: Table using <b> for headers instead of <th>
common_failures.impact: Screen readers cannot associate data with headers

common_failures.example: Label text near input but not using <label> element
common_failures.impact: Screen readers don't announce what input is for

success_criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
success_criteria.description: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.
success_criteria.intent: To enable a screen reader to present content in a meaningful order even when the visual layout changes the order.

sufficient: Ordering content in DOM to match meaningful sequence (G57)
Using CSS positioning without affecting DOM order (C27)
Specifying reading order via tabindex when necessary (H34)
advisory: Using CSS flexbox and grid with proper order
failures: Using CSS to reorder content in a way that affects meaning (F1, F49)
Using white space or layout tables to control visual presentation (F32, F33, F34)

test_procedures: Disable CSS and verify content order makes sense
Use screen reader to check reading order
Tab through page and verify focus order is logical
Linearize content and verify it maintains meaning

common_failures.example: Visual order: 1,2,3 but DOM order: 2,1,3
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users experience confusing order

common_failures.example: DOM goes down column 1 then column 2, but should alternate

success_criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
success_criteria.description: Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that all users can access instructions for using content, including users who are blind, have low vision, or are colorblind.

sufficient: Providing textual identification in addition to sensory characteristics (G96)
advisory: Providing text alternatives for location-based cues
failures: Identifying content only by shape or location (F14, F26)
Using color alone to convey information (F73, F81)

test_procedures: Review all instructions for sensory-only references
Check that instructions work without color perception
Verify instructions work without visual reference
Test with screen reader to confirm instructions are understandable

common_failures.example: Click the green button to continue
Click the round button
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users don't perceive shape

common_failures.example: See information on the right
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users don't perceive spatial layout

success_criteria.name: Orientation
success_criteria.description: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, such as portrait or landscape, unless a specific display orientation is essential.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that content displays and functions in any orientation unless a specific orientation is necessary.

sufficient: Using CSS to allow both orientations (G214)
Not locking display orientation via platform features
advisory: Using responsive design for all orientations
Testing in both portrait and landscape modes
failures: Locking orientation without essential need (F97, F100)

test_procedures: Rotate device to portrait and landscape
Verify all content is accessible in both orientations
Check that no orientation is locked unless essential
Test all functionality in both orientations

common_failures.example: Mobile app only works in portrait mode
common_failures.impact: Users with mounted devices cannot access content

common_failures.example: Important content not visible in landscape orientation
common_failures.impact: Users must rotate device to access content

success_criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
success_criteria.description: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined when the input field serves a purpose identified in the Input Purposes for User Interface Components section of WCAG 2.2.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that the purpose of form input fields can be understood by user agents and assistive technologies, enabling them to present and auto-fill form fields in ways that are customized to the user.

sufficient: Using HTML autocomplete attribute (H98)
Using appropriate autocomplete values for common fields (email, name, address, phone, etc.)
advisory: Using ARIA for custom form controls
Providing consistent input purposes across site
failures: Not using autocomplete for common user information fields (F107)

test_procedures: Identify all input fields collecting user information
Verify autocomplete attribute is used with appropriate values
Test that browser/assistive tech can auto-fill fields
Check autocomplete values match WCAG list

common_failures.example: <input type='email'> missing autocomplete='email'
Using autocomplete='name' instead of autocomplete='given-name' and 'family-name'

guidelines.name: Distinguishable
guidelines.description: Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background.

success_criteria.name: Use of Color
success_criteria.description: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that all users, including users with color vision deficiencies, can access information that is conveyed by color differences.

sufficient: Using text or icons in addition to color (G14, G182, G111)
Providing additional visual cue besides color (G138)
advisory: Using sufficient contrast in addition to color
Using patterns in addition to color
failures: Identifying required fields only by color (F73, F81)
Using color alone to distinguish links (F73)
Using only color to convey information in charts (F81)

test_procedures: View page in grayscale and verify all information is still available
Check that required fields are marked with asterisk or text, not just color
Verify links are distinguishable without color (underline, icon, etc.)
Check that color-coded information has text labels or patterns
Test with color blindness simulator

common_failures.issue: Required fields only shown in red
common_failures.example: Red asterisk with no text indication
common_failures.impact: Colorblind users cannot identify required fields

common_failures.example: Green for success, red for error with no icons or text
Bar chart with only color distinguishing data series

success_criteria.name: Audio Control
success_criteria.description: If any audio on a Web page plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, either a mechanism is available to pause or stop the audio, or a mechanism is available to control audio volume independently from the overall system volume level.
success_criteria.intent: To allow a person using a screen reader to hear the screen reader without interference from auto-playing audio.

sufficient: Providing a control to turn off auto-playing audio (G60, G170)
Playing audio for 3 seconds or less (G171)
failures: Auto-playing audio longer than 3 seconds with no control (F23, F93)

test_procedures: Identify any audio that plays automatically on page load
If audio plays longer than 3 seconds, verify pause/stop control exists
Check that control is near top of page or clearly visible
Verify control is keyboard accessible
Test that volume can be controlled independently

common_failures.example: Site plays music automatically with no pause button
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users cannot hear their assistive technology

common_failures.example: Hero video plays with sound on page load

success_criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
success_criteria.description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for large text (at least 18pt or 14pt bold) which requires 3:1, and incidental text (inactive UI components, pure decoration, invisible, or part of picture with significant other visual content).
success_criteria.intent: To provide enough contrast between text and its background so that it can be read by people with moderately low vision.

sufficient: Ensuring sufficient contrast ratio (G18, G148, G174)
Using sufficient contrast for images of text (G145)
advisory: Using higher contrast ratios than minimum
failures: Text has insufficient contrast with background (F24, F83)

test_procedures: Use color contrast analyzer tool to test all text
Verify normal text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Verify large text has at least 3:1 contrast ratio
Check text over images and gradients
Test all UI component text and icons
Verify link text has sufficient contrast

common_failures.issue: Light gray text on white background
common_failures.example: #999999 on #FFFFFF (2.8:1 contrast)
common_failures.impact: Low vision users cannot read text

common_failures.example: Gray placeholder text below 4.5:1
White text over light image

success_criteria.name: Resize Text
success_criteria.description: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that visually rendered text can be scaled successfully without requiring assistive technology.

sufficient: Using relative units for font sizes (C28, C12, C13, C14)
Ensuring text containers resize when text is resized (SCR34)
Not using absolute units for font sizes (avoiding px for font-size)
failures: Using fixed-size text that cannot scale (F69, F80, F94)
Text clipped when zoomed (F94)

test_procedures: Zoom browser to 200% using Ctrl/Cmd +
Verify all text is still visible and readable
Check that no text is cut off or overlaps
Verify all functionality still works
Check horizontal scrolling is not required (unless for tables/complex layouts)
Test that text containers expand with content

common_failures.issue: Fixed height containers cut off text
common_failures.example: Button with height:30px crops text when zoomed
Absolute positioned elements overlap text at 200%
Page requires horizontal scrolling at 200% zoom

success_criteria.name: Images of Text
success_criteria.description: If the technologies being used can achieve the visual presentation, text is used to convey information rather than images of text except for customizable images of text and essential images (like logos).
success_criteria.intent: To encourage authors to enable text presentation that can be adjusted to meet user needs.

sufficient: Using text rather than images of text (G140)
Using CSS to style text instead of images (C22, C30)
advisory: Using CSS web fonts instead of images
Using SVG for logos that need to scale
failures: Using images of text when text could be used (F3)

test_procedures: Identify all images of text
Determine if same presentation could be achieved with styled text
Verify essential images (logos, required visual presentation) are exceptions
Check if customizable alternatives are provided

common_failures.example: Fancy font heading saved as PNG
common_failures.impact: Cannot be resized, translated, or customized

common_failures.example: Button background contains text
common_failures.impact: Text cannot scale or be translated

success_criteria.name: Reflow
success_criteria.description: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions for vertical content at width of 320 CSS pixels and horizontal content at height of 256 CSS pixels, except for parts that require two-dimensional layout (like maps, diagrams, video, games, presentations, data tables, interfaces where keeping toolbars visible is essential).
success_criteria.intent: To support people with low vision who need to enlarge text and read it in a single column by allowing content to reflow.

sufficient: Using responsive design techniques (C32, C31, C33, C38)
Using CSS Flexbox and Grid (C34, C36)
Using media queries for responsive layout (C40)
advisory: Avoiding fixed positioning that prevents reflow
failures: Fixed width content that doesn't reflow (F102)
Content requires 2D scrolling at mobile viewport (F69)

test_procedures: Set browser width to 1280px and zoom to 400% (equivalent to 320px)
Verify content reflows to single column
Check no horizontal scrolling is required
Verify all content and functionality is available
Test responsive design at mobile viewport sizes

common_failures.example: Desktop layout maintained at all sizes requiring horizontal scroll
common_failures.impact: Low vision users must scroll in two dimensions

common_failures.example: Text overlaps at narrow viewport

success_criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
success_criteria.description: The visual presentation of user interface components and graphical objects have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors for UI components (active controls, their states, and focus indicators) and graphical objects (parts of graphics required to understand content).
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that people with moderately low vision can perceive user interface components and meaningful graphics.

sufficient: Ensuring 3:1 contrast for UI components (G195, G207)
Providing sufficient contrast for graphical objects (G174, G183)
advisory: Providing multiple visual cues beyond color
failures: UI component has insufficient contrast (F78)
Graphical object has insufficient contrast (F78)

test_procedures: Use contrast analyzer on UI components (buttons, form controls, focus indicators)
Check contrast of icons and graphical indicators
Verify 3:1 minimum contrast for component boundaries
Test focus indicators for visibility
Check controls in different states (hover, active, disabled)

common_failures.example: Button border #DDDDDD on #FFFFFF (1.3:1)
Light blue outline on white (2.1:1)
Gray icon on light gray (2.5:1)

success_criteria.name: Text Spacing
success_criteria.description: No loss of content or functionality occurs when users adjust line height to 1.5x font size, paragraph spacing to 2x font size, letter spacing to 0.12x font size, and word spacing to 0.16x font size.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that people with low vision or reading disabilities can adjust text spacing to improve readability without loss of content or functionality.

sufficient: Allowing text spacing adjustments without loss of content (C36, C35, C8, C21)
advisory: Not using fixed heights for text containers
failures: Content clipped with text spacing adjustments (F104, F105)

test_procedures: Apply text spacing bookmarklet or extension
Set line-height to 1.5em, paragraph spacing to 2em, letter-spacing to 0.12em, word-spacing to 0.16em
Verify no text is cut off
Check that no content overlaps
Verify all functionality still works

common_failures.example: Card with height:200px clips text with increased spacing
common_failures.impact: Users cannot read full content with adjusted spacing

common_failures.example: Increased line height causes text to overlap below

success_criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
success_criteria.description: Where receiving and then removing pointer hover or keyboard focus triggers additional content to become visible and then hidden, the following are true: Dismissible (can dismiss without moving focus/hover), Hoverable (pointer can move to additional content), Persistent (stays visible until hover/focus removed, dismissed, or invalid).
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that additional content that appears on hover or focus can be perceived and dismissed by users, particularly those with low vision who use screen magnification.

sufficient: Implementing dismiss mechanism like ESC key (SCR39)
Ensuring additional content can be hovered (G212)
Ensuring content persists until dismissed (G201)
advisory: Using ARIA live regions for notifications
failures: Tooltip disappears when trying to hover over it (F95)
No way to dismiss popup without moving focus (F89)

test_procedures: Trigger all hover/focus content (tooltips, submenus, etc.)
Verify ESC key dismisses additional content
Check that pointer can move to additional content without it disappearing
Verify content persists until explicitly dismissed or focus moved away
Test with keyboard and mouse

common_failures.example: Tooltip vanishes when trying to hover over it to read
common_failures.impact: Low vision users using magnification cannot read tooltip

common_failures.example: Popup has no dismiss mechanism except moving mouse
common_failures.impact: Users cannot dismiss content to see underlying text

principles.name: Operable
principles.description: User interface components and navigation must be operable.

guidelines.name: Keyboard Accessible
guidelines.description: Make all functionality available from a keyboard.

success_criteria.name: Keyboard
success_criteria.description: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that, wherever possible, content can be operated through a keyboard or keyboard interface (enabling alternative keyboards, voice input, etc.).

sufficient: Ensuring all functionality is keyboard accessible (G202)
Using standard HTML controls (H91)
Providing keyboard shortcuts (G90)
failures: Requiring mouse-specific events (F54, F55)
Using device-dependent event handlers (F42)

test_procedures: Unplug mouse or avoid using mouse completely
Tab through entire page
Verify all interactive elements are reachable
Test all functionality works with keyboard only
Check custom widgets work with keyboard
Verify no keyboard traps exist

common_failures.example: div with onclick but not keyboard accessible
Menu only opens on hover with no keyboard equivalent
Reordering only works with mouse drag

success_criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
success_criteria.description: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component of the page using a keyboard interface, then focus can be moved away from that component using only a keyboard interface, and if it requires more than unmodified arrow or tab keys or other standard exit methods, the user is advised of the method for moving focus away.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that users can navigate to all areas of content using keyboard and do not get trapped in any subset of content.

sufficient: Ensuring no keyboard trap exists (G21)
Providing standard exit methods or documenting custom methods (G90)
advisory: Using standard HTML controls that manage focus properly
Testing keyboard navigation through all interactive elements
failures: Creating a keyboard trap (F10)

test_procedures: Tab to each interactive element
Verify Tab/Shift+Tab can move focus away
Check modal dialogs can be exited with keyboard
Test that focus doesn't get stuck in any widget
Verify ESC key works for dismissing overlays

common_failures.example: Modal has no close button and ESC doesn't work
Rich text editor prevents Tab from leaving

success_criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
success_criteria.description: If a keyboard shortcut is implemented using only character keys (letter, punctuation, number, or symbol), then at least one of the following is true: can be turned off, can be remapped, or is only active when component has focus.
success_criteria.intent: To reduce accidental activation of keyboard shortcuts and provide flexibility for users who rely on voice input or have physical disabilities.

sufficient: Providing mechanism to turn off single-key shortcuts (G217)
Providing mechanism to remap shortcuts (G216)
Making shortcuts active only when component focused (SCR43)
advisory: Avoiding single-key shortcuts for common letters
failures: Single-key shortcut cannot be turned off or remapped (F99)

test_procedures: Identify all character-key shortcuts
Verify they can be turned off in settings
Check if they can be remapped
Test if they only work when component has focus
Test with voice input software for conflicts

common_failures.example: 's' key triggers search from anywhere on page
common_failures.impact: Voice input users trigger shortcuts when speaking

common_failures.example: Character shortcuts with no disable option

guidelines.name: Enough Time
guidelines.description: Provide users enough time to read and use content.

success_criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
success_criteria.description: For each time limit set by the content, the user can turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit before time expires (with exceptions for real-time events, essential time limits, and limits longer than 20 hours).
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that users with disabilities that affect their ability to read or interact quickly have adequate time to complete tasks.

sufficient: Providing mechanism to turn off time limit (G198)
Providing mechanism to adjust time limit (G133)
Providing mechanism to extend time limit (G180, SCR16)
Using scripts to extend time limit before expiry (SCR1)
advisory: Using time limits greater than 20 hours
failures: Using timed redirects (F40, F41, F58)
No way to extend or disable timeout (F16)

test_procedures: Identify all time limits in content
Verify user can turn off, adjust, or extend each limit
Check that warning appears before timeout with option to extend
Test that essential actions (like auctions) document time requirements
Verify session timeouts can be extended

common_failures.example: User logged out after 15 minutes with no extension option
common_failures.impact: Users lose work if they need more time

common_failures.example: Test has fixed time limit that cannot be extended
common_failures.impact: Users with disabilities cannot complete test

success_criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
success_criteria.description: For moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds, and is presented in parallel with other content, there is a mechanism to pause, stop, or hide it, or control its frequency. For auto-updating information, there is a mechanism to pause, stop, hide, or control update frequency unless it is essential.
success_criteria.intent: To avoid distracting users, especially those with attention deficits, from being able to use the rest of the page.

sufficient: Providing pause mechanism for moving content (G4)
Providing stop mechanism for auto-updating (G186, G191)
Using scripts to control blinking (SCR22, SCR33)
Allowing user to set update frequency (G187)
failures: Auto-playing movement with no pause (F16, F47, F50)
Scrolling content with no pause (F4, F7)

test_procedures: Identify moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating content
Verify content lasting >5 seconds has pause/stop control
Check control is easily findable
Test that pausing doesn't lose information
Verify auto-updating content can be controlled

common_failures.example: Auto-rotating slides with no stop button
common_failures.impact: Users cannot read content before it changes

common_failures.example: Continuous scrolling with no pause control
Live data updates with no way to pause

guidelines.name: Seizures and Physical Reactions
guidelines.description: Do not design content in a way that is known to cause seizures or physical reactions.

success_criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
success_criteria.description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period, or the flash is below the general flash and red flash thresholds.
success_criteria.intent: To prevent photosensitive epileptic seizures caused by flashing.

sufficient: Ensuring no content flashes more than 3 times per second (G19)
Ensuring flash is below general and red flash thresholds (G176)
advisory: Avoiding fully saturated reds in flashing content
failures: Content flashes more than 3 times per second (F1, F3)

test_procedures: Identify any flashing content
Use tool to measure flash frequency
Verify flashing is 3 times per second or less
Check flash size and contrast meet threshold requirements
Test animations for rapid flashing

common_failures.example: Strobe effect or rapid color changes
common_failures.impact: Can trigger seizures in photosensitive users

common_failures.example: Content includes footage with rapid flashes

guidelines.name: Navigable
guidelines.description: Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are.

success_criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
success_criteria.description: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple Web pages.
success_criteria.intent: To allow people who navigate sequentially through content more direct access to primary content of the Web page.

sufficient: Providing skip links (G1, G123, G124)
Using ARIA landmarks (ARIA11)
Using HTML5 sectioning elements (H69)
Providing heading structure for navigation (H70)
failures: No mechanism to skip navigation (F44)

test_procedures: Tab as first action on page
Verify skip link appears and is functional
Check that skip link goes to main content
Test with screen reader that landmarks are present
Verify keyboard can bypass repeated blocks

common_failures.example: Page with navigation but no skip to content link
common_failures.impact: Keyboard users must tab through entire navigation

common_failures.example: Skip link present but focus doesn't move

success_criteria.name: Page Titled
success_criteria.description: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.
success_criteria.intent: To help users find content and orient themselves within it by ensuring that each Web page has a descriptive and informative title.

sufficient: Providing descriptive titles using title element (G88, H25)
advisory: Providing useful page titles for bookmarking
failures: No title element (F25)
Title doesn't describe page (F25)

test_procedures: Check every page has title element
Verify title describes page content or purpose
Check title is unique within site section
Test that title appears in browser tab/window
Verify screen reader announces title

common_failures.example: <title>Page</title> or <title>Untitled</title>
All pages titled 'Company Name'
common_failures.impact: Users cannot distinguish pages in tabs or history

common_failures.example: No title element in head

success_criteria.name: Focus Order
success_criteria.description: If a Web page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that users who navigate sequentially through content encounter information in an order that is consistent with the meaning of the content.

sufficient: Ordering content in DOM to match focus order (G59)
Using tabindex to specify focus order when needed (H4)
Using CSS to position content without affecting DOM order (C27)
failures: Tabindex creates illogical focus order (F44, F85)
Focus order doesn't follow reading order (F85)

test_procedures: Tab through entire page
Verify focus order matches logical reading order
Check focus doesn't jump unexpectedly
Test modal dialogs maintain logical focus order
Verify dynamic content maintains focus order

common_failures.example: Tab goes from top nav to footer then back to content
common_failures.impact: Keyboard users confused by focus order

common_failures.example: tabindex='1' on button breaks natural order
common_failures.impact: Focus order doesn't match visual order

success_criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
success_criteria.description: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined link context, except where the purpose of the link would be ambiguous to users in general.
success_criteria.intent: To help users understand the purpose of each link so they can decide whether they want to follow the link.

sufficient: Providing descriptive link text (G91, G53)
Using alt attribute with link context (H30)
Combining adjacent text with link (H33, H77, H78, H79, H81)
Using ARIA label or labelledby (ARIA7, ARIA8)
failures: Using generic link text without context (F84, F89)

test_procedures: Review all links on page
Verify each link's purpose is clear from text or context
Check no generic 'click here' or 'more' links
Test with screen reader link list
Verify icon-only links have appropriate alternative text

common_failures.example: 'Click here' or 'Read more' without context
common_failures.impact: Users don't know where link goes

common_failures.example: Multiple 'Learn more' links to different destinations
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users cannot distinguish links

common_failures.example: Icon link with no alternative text
common_failures.impact: Link purpose unknown to screen readers

success_criteria.name: Multiple Ways
success_criteria.description: More than one way is available to locate a Web page within a set of Web pages except where the Web Page is the result of, or a step in, a process.
success_criteria.intent: To make it possible for users to locate content in a manner that best meets their needs by providing more than one method.

sufficient: Providing navigation links (G125, G64, G63)
Providing search functionality (G161, G126)
Providing site map (G185, G161, G126)
Providing table of contents (G63)
Providing breadcrumb trail (G65, G128)
failures: Only one way to find pages

test_procedures: Identify at least two ways to reach each page
Verify navigation menu is present
Check if search function exists
Look for site map or table of contents
Check for breadcrumb navigation

common_failures.example: Site has navigation but no search
common_failures.impact: Users who prefer searching cannot find content easily

common_failures.example: Only navigation available with no overview
common_failures.impact: Users cannot see full site structure

success_criteria.name: Headings and Labels
success_criteria.description: Headings and labels clearly and accurately describe their topic or purpose, helping users understand what content follows or what action to take.
success_criteria.intent: To help users understand what information is contained in Web pages and how that information is organized.

sufficient: Providing descriptive headings (G130, G131)
Providing descriptive labels (G131)
advisory: Providing informative labels for form controls
failures: Using non-descriptive headings (F43)

test_procedures: Review all headings for descriptiveness
Check form labels clearly describe purpose
Verify headings accurately describe following content
Test that labels help users understand what input is expected

common_failures.example: 'Section 1', 'Section 2' instead of descriptive text
common_failures.impact: Users don't know what content is about

common_failures.example: 'Input 1' instead of 'Email Address'
common_failures.impact: Users don't know what to enter

success_criteria.name: Focus Visible
success_criteria.description: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.
success_criteria.intent: To help a person know which element has the keyboard focus.

sufficient: Not hiding focus indicator (G149, G165, G195)
Providing highly visible focus indicator (C15, SCR31)
advisory: Making focus indicator thick enough to see
failures: Removing focus indicator without providing visible alternative (F78)
Focus indicator not visible against background (F55)

test_procedures: Tab through all interactive elements
Verify focus indicator is visible on each element
Check focus indicator has sufficient contrast
Test on light and dark backgrounds
Verify focus not hidden by outline:none without replacement

common_failures.example: CSS removes outline with no custom focus style
Light blue outline on white background
1px dotted outline

success_criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
success_criteria.description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
success_criteria.intent: The purpose of this Success Criterion is to ensure that a user interface component that has keyboard focus is not entirely hidden by content created by the author. When navigating with a keyboard, users need to be able to see the component that currently has focus. People with attention limitations, short-term memory limitations, or limitations in executive processes benefit by being able to discover where the focus is located.

sufficient: Ensuring focus is not obscured by sticky headers or footers
Using CSS overflow and positioning to prevent obscuring focused elements
Ensuring dialogs and popups do not obscure focused elements
advisory: Ensuring sufficient spacing between interactive elements and fixed content
Using z-index appropriately to maintain focus visibility
Testing focus visibility with common viewport sizes
failures: Sticky headers or footers that obscure focused elements (F110)
Modal dialogs that cover focused elements without moving focus
Fixed positioned content that overlays focused elements

test_procedures: Tab through all interactive elements on the page
Check that when each element receives focus, at least part of the focus indicator is visible
Test with sticky headers, footers, and other fixed-position content
Verify that focus is not completely hidden by author-created content
Test at various viewport sizes to ensure focus remains visible

common_failures.example: Fixed header at top of page covers focused links when scrolled into view
common_failures.impact: Keyboard users cannot see which element has focus

common_failures.example: Cookie consent banner at bottom covers focused buttons
Persistent navigation sidebar obscures focused form fields
common_failures.impact: Users lose track of current focus position

guidelines.name: Input Modalities
guidelines.description: Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard.

success_criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
success_criteria.description: All functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures for operation can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture, unless a multipoint or path-based gesture is essential.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that content can be operated by users with various disabilities who cannot perform complex pointer gestures.

sufficient: Providing alternatives to complex gestures (G215, G216)
advisory: Using simple tap/click for all functionality
failures: No alternative to multipoint gesture (F105)

test_procedures: Identify all gesture-based functionality
Verify single-pointer alternative exists
Test that complex gestures are not required
Check pinch-to-zoom has +/- button alternative
Verify swipe actions have button alternatives

common_failures.example: No +/- buttons for zooming map
common_failures.impact: Users with mobility impairments cannot zoom

common_failures.example: Gallery requires swipe with no next/previous buttons

success_criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
success_criteria.description: For functionality that can be operated using a single pointer, at least one of the following is true: no down-event is used, completion is on up-event with ability to abort, up-event reverses any outcome of down-event, or completing on down-event is essential.
success_criteria.intent: To make it easier for users to prevent accidental or erroneous pointer input.

sufficient: Triggering on up-event (G210, G212)
Providing ability to abort or undo (G210, G212)
advisory: Using click event rather than mousedown
failures: Activating on down-event without ability to abort (F101)

test_procedures: Test all clickable elements
Press and hold pointer on element then drag away
Verify action doesn't complete if pointer moved away
Check actions occur on release, not on press
Verify ability to abort accidental activations

common_failures.example: Button activates on press instead of release
Drag operation completes with no abort option

success_criteria.name: Label in Name
success_criteria.description: For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the name contains the text that is presented visually.
success_criteria.intent: To help speech input users interact with components by ensuring the visible label matches the accessible name.

sufficient: Using visible label text in accessible name (G208, G211)
advisory: Starting accessible name with visible label
Using same text for visible and accessible name
failures: Accessible name doesn't include visible label text (F96)

test_procedures: Identify all labeled components
Check accessible name includes visible label text
Verify speech input can target using visible label
Use browser inspector to check accessible name
Test with speech input software

common_failures.example: Button shows 'Search' but aria-label='Find'
common_failures.impact: Voice input users saying 'Search' won't activate button

common_failures.issue: Icon button accessible name doesn't include visible text
common_failures.example: Button shows 'Save' icon and text but accessible name is only 'icon'

success_criteria.name: Motion Actuation
success_criteria.description: Functionality that can be operated by device motion or user motion can also be operated by user interface components and responding to the motion can be disabled to prevent accidental actuation.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that functionality triggered by device motion (shaking, tilting) or user motion (waving) can also be operated through accessible user interface components, and can be disabled.

sufficient: Providing button alternatives to motion actuation (G213)
Providing settings to disable motion actuation (G213)
advisory: Providing clear indication when motion is being used
failures: No alternative to motion actuation (F106)

test_procedures: Identify all motion-actuated functionality
Verify button or control alternative exists
Check settings allow disabling motion actuation
Test that functionality still works with motion disabled

common_failures.example: No button to undo, must shake device
common_failures.impact: Users who cannot shake device cannot undo

common_failures.example: Shake always triggers action even if accidental
common_failures.impact: Users with tremors trigger actions unintentionally

success_criteria.name: Dragging Movements
success_criteria.description: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential or the functionality is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author.
success_criteria.intent: The intent of this Success Criterion is to ensure that functionality that uses a dragging movement (e.g., sliders, drag-and-drop interfaces) has another single pointer mode of operation without the need for the dexterity required to drag elements. Some people cannot perform dragging movements in a precise manner due to hand tremor, limited dexterity, or other reasons. People who use a specialized or adapted input device such as a head pointer, eye-gaze system, or speech-controlled mouse emulator may also find dragging difficult or impossible.

sufficient: Providing single pointer alternatives to dragging movements
Using buttons to move items instead of drag-and-drop
Providing input fields as alternatives to sliders
advisory: Providing both drag-and-drop and cut/paste or keyboard alternatives
Supporting tap to select and tap to place for drag-and-drop
failures: Only supporting drag-and-drop without single pointer alternative
Requiring dragging with no alternative input method

test_procedures: Identify all functionality that uses dragging movements
Verify single pointer alternatives exist (buttons, input fields, etc.)
Test that alternatives achieve the same functionality
Check that sliders can be operated by tapping/clicking at target position
Verify drag-and-drop has keyboard or button-based alternatives

common_failures.example: Volume slider requires dragging with no way to click at position or use increment buttons
common_failures.impact: Users with limited dexterity cannot adjust slider values

common_failures.example: Reordering list items only possible via drag-and-drop
Map interface only allows panning by dragging with no pan buttons

success_criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
success_criteria.description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except where: the target is available through an equivalent link or control on the same page that meets this criterion; the target is inline in a block of text; the size of the target is determined by the user agent and is not modified by the author; a particular presentation of the target is essential or is legally required for the information being conveyed.
success_criteria.intent: The intent of this Success Criterion is to ensure that target sizes are large enough for users to easily activate them, even if they have difficulty with fine motor movements. Touch interfaces, in particular, require larger targets to support users with limited dexterity. Mouse, stylus, or eye-gaze system users can also benefit from larger targets. The 24 by 24 CSS pixel minimum ensures usability for a broad range of users, including people with tremors or other movement disorders.

sufficient: Ensuring inline links provide sufficiently large click targets (C42)
Using CSS to increase the size of small targets
Providing large click targets for pointer input
advisory: Ensuring buttons and links are at least 44x44 CSS pixels for enhanced usability
Making full card areas clickable rather than just text links
failures: Interactive controls smaller than 24x24 CSS pixels without exceptions (F111)

test_procedures: Identify all interactive elements that accept pointer input
Measure the target size (width × height) in CSS pixels
Verify targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels
Check if any exceptions apply (inline text, user agent controlled, essential, etc.)
Test on touch devices to verify usability

common_failures.example: Close button that is only 16x16 CSS pixels
common_failures.impact: Users have difficulty activating small targets, especially on touch devices

common_failures.example: Default HTML checkboxes that are smaller than 24x24 pixels
common_failures.impact: Users struggle to select options accurately

common_failures.example: Navigation menu with links smaller than minimum target size
common_failures.impact: Users frequently mis-tap and activate wrong links

principles.name: Understandable
principles.description: Information and the operation of user interface must be understandable.

guidelines.name: Readable
guidelines.description: Make text content readable and understandable.

success_criteria.name: Language of Page
success_criteria.description: The default human language of each Web page can be programmatically determined.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure screen readers and other assistive technologies can render text correctly by knowing the language of content.

sufficient: Using lang attribute on html element (H57)
failures: No lang attribute on html element (F3)

test_procedures: Check html element has lang attribute
Verify lang value uses valid language code (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr')
Test screen reader uses correct pronunciation

common_failures.example: <html> without lang attribute
lang='english' instead of lang='en'

success_criteria.name: Language of Parts
success_criteria.description: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined except for proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words or phrases that have become part of the vernacular of the immediately surrounding text.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that user agents can correctly present content written in multiple languages.

sufficient: Using lang attribute on elements for language changes (H58)
advisory: Marking up quotes in other languages
failures: Language changes not marked up (F9)

test_procedures: Identify passages in different languages
Verify lang attribute marks language changes
Test screen reader pronunciation changes appropriately

common_failures.example: Spanish quote in English page without lang='es'
French paragraph in English page without language markup

guidelines.name: Predictable
guidelines.description: Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways.

success_criteria.name: On Focus
success_criteria.description: When any user interface component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that functionality is predictable as visitors navigate through a document.

sufficient: Not causing changes on focus (G107)
failures: Launching new window on focus (F52, F55)
Automatically submitting form on focus (F55)

test_procedures: Tab to each interactive element
Verify focus alone doesn't trigger changes
Check no new windows open on focus
Verify forms don't submit on focus

common_failures.example: Help dialog opens when field receives focus
Tabbing to button submits form

success_criteria.name: On Input
success_criteria.description: Changing the setting of any user interface component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised of the behavior before using the component.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that entering data or selecting a form control has predictable effects.

sufficient: Using button to trigger changes (G80, H32, H84)
Warning users before auto-updating (G13)
advisory: Using onchange only with user notification
failures: Automatically changing context on input (F36, F37)

test_procedures: Interact with all form controls
Verify changes don't occur automatically on input
Check dropdowns don't navigate on selection
Verify forms have submit buttons

common_failures.example: Selecting option immediately navigates to new page
Clicking radio submits form immediately
common_failures.impact: Users cannot review choices before submitting

success_criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
success_criteria.description: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple Web pages within a set of Web pages occur in the same relative order each time they are repeated, unless a change is initiated by the user.
success_criteria.intent: To encourage use of consistent navigation across a set of Web pages.

sufficient: Using consistent navigation order (G61)
failures: Navigation order changes on different pages (F66)

test_procedures: Navigate through multiple pages
Verify navigation menu items appear in same order
Check navigation position is consistent
Verify repeated elements maintain order

common_failures.example: Home, About, Contact on one page; About, Home, Contact on another
Top navigation on some pages, side navigation on others

success_criteria.name: Consistent Identification
success_criteria.description: Components that have the same functionality within a set of Web pages are identified consistently.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that components with the same function are identified consistently across pages.

sufficient: Using consistent labels for same function (G197)
advisory: Using consistent icons for same function
failures: Using different labels for same function (F31)

test_procedures: Identify repeated functional components
Verify same labels/icons used consistently
Check search always labeled 'Search'
Verify submit buttons use consistent text

common_failures.example: 'Submit' on one page, 'Send' on another for same function
Trash can icon on one page, X icon on another for delete

success_criteria.name: Consistent Help
success_criteria.description: If a Web page contains any of the following help mechanisms, and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple Web pages within a set of Web pages, they occur in the same relative order to other page content, unless a change is initiated by the user: Human contact details, Human contact mechanism, Self-help option, A fully automated contact mechanism.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure users can easily find help when it is provided, by keeping help mechanisms in a consistent location.

sufficient: Providing help link in consistent location (G220)
Using consistent position for help mechanisms (G221)
advisory: Placing help in header or footer
failures: Help mechanism moves to different location (F108)

test_procedures: Identify help mechanisms across pages
Verify help appears in same position
Check contact info has consistent placement
Test help link location is predictable

common_failures.example: Help in header on one page, footer on another
Contact info top of some pages, bottom of others

guidelines.name: Input Assistance
guidelines.description: Help users avoid and correct mistakes.

success_criteria.name: Error Identification
success_criteria.description: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that users are aware that an error has occurred and can determine what is wrong.

sufficient: Providing text description of error (G83, G84, G85)
Using ARIA alerts for errors (ARIA18, ARIA19, ARIA21)
failures: Using color alone to indicate error (F81, F82)
Not identifying error in text (F3)

test_procedures: Submit forms with errors
Verify errors are identified in text
Check each error field is indicated
Test screen reader announces errors
Verify error not shown by color alone

common_failures.example: Field turns red with no text explanation
common_failures.impact: Users don't know what the error is

common_failures.example: 'Form has errors' without specifying which fields
Visual error but screen reader doesn't announce it
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users unaware of error

success_criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
success_criteria.description: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.
success_criteria.intent: To help users understand what information they should provide in form fields.

sufficient: Providing labels for form controls (G131, G89, G162, G83)
Using label element (H44, H71, H65)
Using title attribute (H65)
Using ARIA labelledby or label (ARIA1, ARIA16, ARIA14)
advisory: Providing help text for complex inputs
failures: Form control without label (F82, F68)

test_procedures: Check all form fields have labels
Verify labels describe purpose clearly
Test screen reader announces labels
Check complex fields have instructions
Verify required fields are indicated

common_failures.example: Input field with placeholder but no label element
Label says 'Input 1' instead of descriptive text
common_failures.impact: Users don't know what to enter

common_failures.example: Date field with no indication of required format
common_failures.impact: Users enter data in wrong format

success_criteria.name: Error Suggestion
success_criteria.description: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, then the suggestions are provided to the user, unless it would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.
success_criteria.intent: To help users understand how to correct input errors when possible.

sufficient: Providing suggestions for correcting errors (G83, G84, G85, G177)
Using ARIA to provide error suggestions (ARIA18, SCR18)
failures: Providing error without suggestion when suggestion possible

test_procedures: Trigger various input errors
Verify suggestions are provided where possible
Check suggestions are specific and helpful
Test that suggestions don't reveal security info

common_failures.example: 'Invalid date' without showing expected format
common_failures.impact: Users don't know how to fix error

common_failures.example: 'Fix the format' without explaining how

success_criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
success_criteria.description: For Web pages that cause legal commitments or financial transactions for the user to occur, that modify or delete user-controllable data in data storage systems, or that submit user test responses, at least one of the following is true: submissions are reversible, data is checked and user given opportunity to correct errors, or mechanism is available for reviewing and confirming information before final submission.
success_criteria.intent: To help users avoid serious consequences resulting from mistakes when performing actions that cannot be reversed.

sufficient: Providing ability to review and correct before submission (G98, G99, G155, G168)
Making actions reversible (G164)
Checking data and providing opportunity to correct (G168)
failures: No prevention for critical actions

test_procedures: Identify legal/financial/data transactions
Verify review step before submission
Check confirmation is required for critical actions
Test that errors are checked before final submission
Verify reversibility or undo for critical actions

common_failures.example: One-click purchase with no confirmation
common_failures.impact: Users cannot review order before committing

common_failures.example: Delete account button with no verification
Financial form submits without validating critical fields
common_failures.impact: Errors not caught before legal commitment

success_criteria.name: Redundant Entry
success_criteria.description: Information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same process is either auto-populated, or available for the user to select.
success_criteria.intent: To reduce cognitive load and errors by not requiring users to re-enter information they have already provided in a process.

sufficient: Auto-populating previously entered data (G221)
Providing option to select previously entered data (G198)
advisory: Using session storage to remember entries
Providing copy from previous step functionality
failures: Requiring re-entry of same information without auto-population (F109)

test_procedures: Complete multi-step process
Note when same information is requested again
Verify information is auto-populated or selectable
Check shipping/billing address scenarios
Test that essential re-entry (like password confirmation) is excluded

common_failures.example: Billing address must be typed again when same as shipping
common_failures.impact: Extra effort and potential for errors

common_failures.example: Email entered in step 1 must be entered again in step 3

success_criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
success_criteria.description: A cognitive function test (such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle) is not required for any step in an authentication process unless that step provides at least one of the following: Alternative (another authentication method not relying on cognitive function test), Mechanism (assistance like password managers available), Object Recognition (cognitive test is recognizing objects), or Personal Content (cognitive test is identifying non-text content user provided).
success_criteria.intent: To ensure people with cognitive disabilities can authenticate to use services.

sufficient: Supporting password managers (G218)
Providing alternative authentication methods (G217, G220)
Using WebAuthn (G220)
Allowing copy/paste in password fields (G218)
failures: Blocking password managers (F109)
Requiring cognitive tests without alternatives (F108)

test_procedures: Attempt to use password manager
Check if alternative authentication methods offered
Verify copy/paste works in password fields
Test that CAPTCHAs have accessible alternatives
Check security questions have object recognition option

common_failures.example: autocomplete='off' prevents password manager
common_failures.impact: Users with memory issues cannot use assistance

common_failures.example: Text-based puzzle with no alternative
common_failures.impact: Users with cognitive disabilities cannot authenticate

common_failures.example: JavaScript prevents pasting password

principles.name: Robust
principles.description: Content must be robust enough that it can be interpreted by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies.

guidelines.name: Compatible
guidelines.description: Maximize compatibility with current and future user agents, including assistive technologies.

success_criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
success_criteria.description: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that assistive technologies can gather information about, activate, and keep up to date on the status of user interface controls in the content.

sufficient: Using standard HTML controls (H91, H44, H64, H88, H90)
Using ARIA roles, states, and properties (ARIA14, ARIA16, G108, ARIA1, ARIA2)
Using title attribute (H65)
failures: Using div or span for buttons without role (F15, F20, F59, F79, F86, F89)

test_procedures: Inspect all UI components with browser developer tools
Verify name (label/text) is programmatically exposed
Check role is correctly identified (button, link, checkbox, etc.)
Test states are exposed (checked, expanded, selected, etc.)

success_criteria.name: Status Messages
success_criteria.description: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
success_criteria.intent: To ensure that status messages can be presented to users who use screen readers and other assistive technologies without requiring the user's focus to move to the message.

sufficient: Using ARIA role='status' (G199, ARIA22)
Using ARIA role='alert' (ARIA19, G193)
Using ARIA live regions (ARIA23, G194)
advisory: Using aria-atomic for complete message reading
failures: Status messages not programmatically determinable (F103, F104)

test_procedures: Trigger all status messages (success, error, progress, etc.)
Verify messages don't receive focus
Check screen reader announces messages
Test ARIA live regions or role='status/alert' are used
Verify important updates are communicated to assistive tech

common_failures.example: Form submission success shown visually but not in ARIA live region
Validation error appears but screen reader not notified
File upload progress shown but not announced
common_failures.impact: Screen reader users don't know progress

how_to_conduct_wcag_audit: 1. Determine conformance level target (A or AA)
2. Test each applicable success criterion systematically
3. Use automated tools for initial scan (but manual testing required)
4. Test with assistive technologies (screen readers, voice input, magnification)
5. Document all failures with specific criterion numbers
6. Prioritize remediation based on severity and user impact
testing_tools: Automated: WAVE, axe DevTools, Lighthouse, Pa11y
Screen readers: NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (Mac/iOS), TalkBack (Android)
Browser extensions: axe, WAVE, Accessibility Insights
Contrast checkers: WebAIM Contrast Checker, Colour Contrast Analyser
Code validators: W3C HTML Validator, ARIA validator

conformance_requirements.level_a: Minimum legal requirement in many jurisdictions. All Level A criteria must pass.
conformance_requirements.level_aa: Recommended target for most websites. Legally required for government sites in many countries. All Level A and AA criteria must pass.
conformance_requirements.conformance_claims: Should specify: conformance level, scope (full site or pages), date, WCAG version

priority_guidance.critical: Level A failures that prevent access (no keyboard access, missing alt text, no captions)
priority_guidance.high: Level AA failures affecting many users (contrast, text resize, focus visible)
priority_guidance.medium: Level AA failures with workarounds (redundant entry, text spacing)
